_comment_product: Campaign / product identity. Printed in the run banner and tells the engine (and downstream n8n) which Visioneerit product this config is for — swap the whole file to run another product.
_comment_one_liner: Plain-English pitch printed at the start of a live run so operators know what this campaign is selling. Not injected into the email body.
one_liner: AI market intelligence for GovCon — who is winning the work, who they team with, and who you already know inside the agency.
_comment_icp: Ideal Customer Profile filters passed to Apollo's free people search. Wrong ICP = wrong leads; the engine does not hardcode titles or geos.

icp._comment_person_titles: Apollo title filters — who we want on the list (capture/BD roles that buy market-intel tools).
icp._comment_person_locations: Apollo geo filter. OryonIQ targets US GovCon buyers only.
icp._comment_q_keywords: Free-text Apollo keyword that narrows results to the buyer's world (beyond title alone).

_comment_signal: The live, dated market hook fed into OpenAI's system prompt. Gives the personalizer a real trigger to ground the opener — keep it current and specific or openers go generic.
signal: The Pentagon suspended CMMC Phase II on July 13, 2026 — third-party assessments are paused pending a 60-day review, while DoD committed $32B to AI, cloud, and cyber in H1 FY2026. The bid barrier just dropped on a lot of money.
_comment_offer: The plain-words paragraph that follows the AI opener in the email, and that fills the `offer` variable on the Sendr page. REWRITTEN 2026-08-29: the previous OryonIQ line was 'maps who's already winning in your NAICS and who they're teaming with' — category jargon (NAICS, maps, teaming) that describes a product category rather than telling the reader what they get. Whatever this says must stay inside oryoniq-product-features.md, and must be re-synced into VIO-sendr-generate-page's ROUTES map with `python3 n8n-workflows/sync-routes.py --fix` or the page and the email argue different cases to the same prospect.
offer: OryonIQ shows you who has been winning the work you bid on, who they teamed with to win it, and whether anyone you already know sits inside the agency deciding it. Award data and relationship data on one map.
_comment_cta: The ask in every email is 'worth fifteen minutes?', so the button a prospect clicks should open the calendar, not a contact form. Same HubSpot link as booking_url: the page embeds the calendar AND offers it as a button. Use THIS PRODUCT'S OWN link — an OryonIQ email that sends the prospect to visioneerit.com reads like a bait-and-switch.
_comment_sender: OryonIQ markets STANDALONE — no parent-company mention anywhere a prospect reads. This was 'OryonIQ (a VisioneerIT company)', and before that 'OryonIQ, VisioneerIT'. Both put a second brand in front of a GovCon buyer who has never heard of either, which spends attention explaining an org chart instead of the offer. Owner's call, 2026-09-01. config-visioneerit.json is unaffected — VisioneerIT signs its own mail.
_comment_personalization_prompt: Per-lead OpenAI task template. Must keep {first_name} and {company} (and usually {title}) so the engine can fill them per prospect. Instructs the model not to invent company facts.
personalization_prompt: Write ONE specific opening line (max 2 sentences) for a cold email to {first_name}, {title} at {company} — a US government contractor. Tie the current signal to their capture/BD reality. Do NOT invent specific facts about {company}; keep it about their role and the signal.
_comment_booking_url: HubSpot Meetings page for OryonIQ (Gavriel's calendar). Verified 2026-09-04: sends NO x-frame-options and NO frame-ancestors, so Sendr's calendar element can embed it — the first embeddable calendar this project has had. The contact pages both block framing; never put one here. A booking on this page is the conversion event: the HubSpot meeting webhook should mark the lead meeting_booked and stop the sequence.
_comment_sendr: The LinkedIn + personalized-page leg. Optional: omit the whole block and the engine skips Sendr entirely. Every id here is a REAL id read from the live Sendr account — see INTEGRATIONS.md. This block is what makes 'one engine, many products' true on the Sendr side: swap the config, get the other product's page and sequence with no code change.

sendr._comment_page_template_id: Sendr page template built in the Sendr UI (Sendr has no create-template API). Its declared variable tags are read live at generate time, so this never needs editing when the template's copy changes.
sendr._comment_campaign_id: The LinkedIn sequence for this product. Read-only from the API — Sendr has no add-lead-to-campaign endpoint, so enrolment stays a human action in the Sendr UI. Recorded here so the operator (and the docs) always know which sequence pairs with which page.
sendr._comment_gif_source: How the GIF preview embedded in the outreach message is rendered. 'dynamic-website' screenshots the LEAD's own site (needs a per-lead URL, highest impact); 'landing-page' previews the generated page itself and needs no extra input, so it is the safe default when a lead has no known domain.
sendr.gif_hyperlink_text: See who has been winning the work you bid on

_comment_claims: Both of these carried the disputed pre-RFP claim until 2026-08-29. one_liner said 'surfaces federal pursuits before the RFP' and gif_hyperlink_text said 'See the 3 pursuits OryonIQ is tracking for your NAICS codes' — pre-RFP alerting, pursuit tracking and NAICS filtering appear NOWHERE on oryoniq.com (see oryoniq-product-features.md). The GIF link text is prospect-facing: it is the caption under the animation in the email and on the Sendr page, so it was the single most visible place the overclaim survived. Both now describe award + relationship data, which is what the product actually does.

opt_out_line: Not interested? Reply "unsubscribe" and I will take you off the list.
_comment_compliance: CAN-SPAM 15 U.S.C. 7704(a)(5) requires every commercial message to carry a valid physical postal address AND a working opt-out. Neither existed in any sendable body until 2026-08-30 — verified across all 10 steps of both campaigns. Liability is per message, so this is not something to add 'before launch'; it has to be in the copy the moment anything can send. The opt-out is REPLY-BASED on purpose rather than a merge tag: VIO-instantly-events already writes an opt_out event to the Suppression tab and VIO-inbound-reply-to-call already detects stop intent in reply text, both with registered webhooks — so this route is known to work, whereas an unverified merge tag can render as a literal token in a real prospect's inbox. Instantly's own insert_unsubscribe_header is turned on alongside it for one-click support. Both strings are mirrored into every campaign body; sync-routes.py's `compliance` check fails if any sendable body loses either one.
_comment_postal_address: CAN-SPAM requires a valid physical postal address in every commercial message. The address is real and unchanged; only the name on it is the product brand, so OryonIQ mail carries no parent-company reference. If counsel wants the registered entity named instead, change this one field and run sync-routes.py --fix — every consumer follows from here.
